//: Manga · the PRINTED PAGE: purely black and white, no hue anywhere.
//1: THE source for every shell surface (quickshell/: bar, launcher, OSD, power
//2: menu). No upstream palette — every role is a grey lifted from the wallpaper,
//3: a black-ink line drawing of a girl in a uniform with blades on a flat
//4: off-white page: the page, the ink, the screentone greys in the shadow.
//5: `tokens` names each role after what it is in the picture so the mapping
//6: stays traceable. theme.lua still owns WINDOW chrome (gaps, border, blur,
//8: No-hue rule: graphite is grey ink on paper with ONE violet, inkwash has gold
//9: and cyan; manga has none — not even for state. Every role is a grey, and
//10: state is told by WEIGHT, not hue: the INK (#111111) is the frame — island
//11: rims, window border, lock ring — the drawing's own ink one weight under it
//12: is every readout, a mid ink is the launcher, and pending (`warn`) and fine
//13: (`ok`) are lighter inks while `urgent` is pure black, the one thing darker
//14: than the frame. A pending count reads as a lighter figure, an overdue one as
//15: a heavier one, and the alert is the pulse Chip.qml draws, not a color. No
//16: readoutBright on purpose, like graphite: the active workspace is then a solid
//17: ink block with the digit in `ground` (modules/Workspaces.qml), a printed
//18: panel number, instead of an emissive lozenge.
name: manga
//tokens: What in the picture -> role, so a palette bump stays traceable. The page is #f5f5f5, the ink is #000, the hair solid black, the screentone greys in the shadow ~#3a3a3a; the lighter inks (pencil, the mid ink, the state greys) are those two ends stepped by weight. warn/ok/urgent are weights, not scenery: pending is a mid grey, fine is the lightest, urgent is the pure ink.
//contrast: Measured (WCAG, sRGB blend) on the three surfaces that carry type: `surface`; the bar island — `#f5f5f5` at 0.94 over the page's top strip (#f6f6f6 measured, flat; composite #f5f5f5); the launcher window — `ground` at 0.96 over the picture's centre (#f6f6f6 → #e9e9e9); and `ground` itself, the terminal. dim 3.4 / 3.4 / 3.0 / 3.0, dormant 4.2 / 4.2 / 3.7 / 3.7, frame 17.3 / 17.3 / 15.6 / 15.4, readout 12.5 / 12.5 / 11.2 / 11.1, launcher 8.1 / 8.1 / 7.3 / 7.2, warn 6.1 / 6.1 / 5.5 / 5.5, ok 3.0 / 3.0 / 2.7 / 2.7, urgent 19.3 / 19.3 / 17.3 / 17.1, text 16.6 / 16.6 / 14.9 / 14.8. `ground` on `frame` (the active workspace's digit) 15.4:1; the launcher's selected row (launcher on its own 18% tint, #cccccc) 5.5:1; `surface` on `launcher` (the terminal's selection, GTK's accent print) 8.1:1.
//quiet: `dim` and `dormant` are two pencil weights, not a weight and a tint: on paper the quiet greys have to be DARKER than they look right, because every surface that carries them is near-white. Both are printed to >= 3:1 on `surface` AND on `ground` (the terminal's bright black is `dim`): dim #858585 (the brief's #8a8a8a was 2.8:1 on cardstock), dormant #767676 — the launcher's secondary type, 3.7:1 on its window. `ok` is the lightest state and still carries type (the charging percentage, a Spotify title), so it too is printed down to 3.0:1 on the page (#8e8e8e; #9a9a9a was 2.6:1) — one step lighter than `dim`, and never on cardstock.
//effects: A printed page: no glow (ink does not emit); screentone rides every panel — a grid of `frame` ink dots, one every 4px, offset every other row (components/Texture.qml `halftone`). 0.12 over the kind's resting 0.10: the fill is near-opaque white and at 1.5x the dots have to read as tone, not vanish.
//bar: Bar identity. Printed panels: the clean page (surface) at 0.94 — near-opaque on purpose, a line drawing frosted through a light fill just goes grey, so the fill is page and the drawing stays outside it — with a 1px INK rim at 90% (an inked panel border, heavier than graphite's 70% pencil rim) and 4px corners: a printed panel's corner is nearly square. gruvbox is 4 too, but gruvbox is a dark CRT. No accent line, no bloom.
//launcher: Launcher identity: a 1px mid-ink frame (`launcher`, the one surface that covers the bar gets the one weight the bar never uses) around cardstock at 0.96, 4px window (the one corner), 3px input + rows (the chips' corner). The selected row is the mid ink on its own 18% tint: 5.5:1.
//osd: OSD identity: a 4px slab, not a pill — nothing on a printed page is a lozenge — with a 1px ink frame and a track in the drawing's ink (readout).
//session: Power-menu identity: page tiles with 4px corners (the one corner) and a 1px ink edge at 90% (the inked panel border), over a 0.85 cardstock scrim — the page goes to blank paper behind the menu.
//wallpaper: Shared by hyprlock.conf (brightness) and sddm/Main.qml (1 - brightness scrim). 0.95, not 0.55: graphite's reasoning — the picture is an off-white page, and dimming paper makes slate. Barely under 1 at all, because this page is flatter and whiter than graphite's sketch paper: the lock and the greeter are read as ink on paper.
